newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gerling Global Re aims to grow abroad.
newsitem.headline: Gerling Global Re aims to grow abroad.

text.p: German insurer Gerling-Konzern Globale Rueckversicherungs-AG (GKG) said on Thursday it wanted to grow especially in foreign markets.
"We see enormous growth in Asia and Latin America," GKG managing director Norbert Strohschen told a news conference.
Strohschen said there was less pressure on premium levels in those regions.
In the 1995/96 business year to June 30, GKG saw a growth in premiums of 3.9 percent to 4.009 billion marks from 3.857 billion marks the previous year.
Net profit fell to 38.93 million marks from 213.58 million marks, although last year GKG's profits were boosted by an extraordinary profit from the sale of its interest in Frankona Rueckversicherung.
Without this effect Gerling would have earned only 18.1 million marks last year, the company said.

This year, Strohschen said, results should be steady adding the dividend had been raised by three percentage points to 15 percent. A consideration in this was the firm's capital improvement of 88.750 million marks to 325 million marks.
He added that the absence of natural disasters with large insurance damages had pushed premiums down, but the company had declined to increase growth through concessions on premium levels.
The loss on its insurance business improved to 139.5 million marks from 222.8 million marks, despite several large damages from fluctuation provisions.
Including provisions, the loss in this area was 253.8 million marks, better than the 294.3 million marks last year.
Total business profit was down at 323.89 million marks, from 563.93 million marks the year before, because of the Frankona effect.

The GKG parent, which owns a series of foreign businesses, had a total turnover of 4.559 billion marks, up from 4.382 billion last year and made profit of 71 million marks, down from 214 million marks last year.
The company said premium income should grow to seven billion marks by the year 2001.
